title: Mastering Section 50C: Stamp Duty Value as Deemed Consideration
subject: DT
provision_raw: Section 50C: Where consideration received on transfer of land or building is less than the stamp duty value assessed by stamp valuation authority, such stamp duty value shall be deemed to be the full value of consideration.
story_summary: Rahul sells a commercial plot in Kochi to Anita for an agreed price of ₹40 Lakhs. However, the State Stamp Valuation Authority assesses the Stamp Duty Value (SDV) of the land at ₹60 Lakhs. Under Section 50C, because the agreed price is lower than the SDV, the Income Tax Department deems ₹60 Lakhs as the Full Value of Consideration for computing Capital Gains.

Here, Agreed Consideration (₹40L) is lower than SDV (₹60L). Scale tilt aakukayum SDV override cheyyukayum cheyyunnu!

slides.slide_title: Statutory Rule & Final Capital Gains Impact
slides.scene_purpose: Statutory Takeaway: Highlighting Section 50C deeming provision
slides.dialogue_manglish: So simple rule: Land or Building transfer cheyyumbol, consideration received SDV-nekkal kuravanenkil, Stamp Duty Value shall be deemed to be the Full Value of Consideration. Capital Gains compute cheyyenda FVC ₹60 Lakhs aayirikkum!

slots.title: Section 50C Core Mandate
slots.statement: Where consideration received on transfer of land or building is less than Stamp Duty Value, such Stamp Duty Value is DEEMED as Full Value of Consideration.
slots.highlight_phrase: Stamp Duty Value is DEEMED as Full Value of Consideration
slots.support_line: Rahul must compute Capital Gains using ₹60 Lakhs as FVC instead of ₹40 Lakhs.
